{{short description|Probability distribution}}
{{expert needed|statistics|reason=New article adapted from NIST document, needs checking and expansion by someone familiar with the topic|date=August 2015}}
{{Infobox probability distribution
|name=Wakeby distribution
|parameters=<math>\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta, \xi</math>
|quantile=<math>\xi + \frac{\alpha}{\beta}(1 - (1-p)^{\beta}) - \frac{\gamma}{\delta}(1 - (1-p)^{-\delta})</math>
|support=<math>\xi </math> to <math>\infty</math>, if <math>\delta \ge 0, \gamma > 0</math>
<math>\xi </math> to  <math>\xi + (\alpha/ \beta) - (\gamma/ \delta) </math>, otherwise
|type=density
}}

The '''Wakeby distribution'''<ref name=WAKPDF>{{cite web|url= http://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/software/dataplot/refman2/auxillar/wakpdf.htm|title=Dataplot reference manual: WAKPDF |publisher=NIST|access-date=20 August 2015}}</ref> is a five-parameter [[probability distribution]] defined by its quantile function,

:<math>W(p) =\xi + \frac{\alpha}{\beta}(1 - (1-p)^{\beta}) - \frac{\gamma}{\delta}(1 - (1-p)^{-\delta})</math>,

and by its quantile density function,

:<math>W'(p) = w(p) = \alpha (1-p)^{\beta - 1} + \gamma (1-p)^{-\delta - 1}</math>,

where <math>0 \le p \le 1</math>, &xi; is a [[location parameter]], &alpha; and &gamma; are scale parameters and 
&beta; and &delta; are [[shape parameter]]s.<ref name="WAKPDF" />

This distribution was first proposed by John C. Houghton while under the supervision of Harold A. Thomas Jr.,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Houghton |first=John C. |date=December 1978 |title=Birth of a Parent: The Wakeby Distribution for Modeling Flood Flows |url=https://doi.org/10.1029/WR014i006p01105 |journal=Water Resources Research |volume=14 |issue=6 |pages=1105-1109 |via=AGU}}</ref> who named it after [[Wakeby Pond]] in [[Cape Cod]].<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Rodda|first1=John C.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=DzV0CgAAQBAJ&q=%22wakeby+pond%22|title=Progress in Modern Hydrology: Past, Present and Future|last2=Robinson|first2=Mark|date=2015-08-26|publisher=John Wiley & Sons|isbn=978-1-119-07429-8|page=75|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Katchanov|first1=Yurij L.|last2=Markova|first2=Yulia V.|date=2015-02-26|title=On a heuristic point of view concerning the citation distribution: introducing the Wakeby distribution|journal=SpringerPlus|language=en|volume=4|issue=1|page=94|doi=10.1186/s40064-015-0821-1|issn=2193-1801|pmc=4352413|pmid=25763305 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

== Applications ==
The Wakeby distribution has been used for modeling distributions of

* flood flows,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dspace.mit.edu/bitstream/handle/1721.1/31278/mit-el-77-033wp-04146753.pdf?sequence=1|title=Birth of a Parent: The Wakeby Distribution for Modeling Flood Flows; Working Paper No. MIT-EL77-033WP|author=John C. Houghton|date=October 14, 1977|publisher=MIT}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=GRIFFITHS|first=GEORGE A.|date=1989-06-01|title=A theoretically based Wakeby distribution for annual flood series|journal=Hydrological Sciences Journal|volume=34|issue=3|pages=231–248|doi=10.1080/02626668909491332|bibcode=1989HydSJ..34..231G |issn=0262-6667}}</ref> 
* citation counts,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Katchanov|first1=Yurij L.|last2=Markova|first2=Yulia V.|date=2015-02-26|title=On a heuristic point of view concerning the citation distribution: introducing the Wakeby distribution|journal=SpringerPlus|language=En|volume=4|issue=1|page=94|doi=10.1186/s40064-015-0821-1|pmid=25763305|issn=2193-1801|pmc=4352413 |doi-access=free }}</ref>
* extreme [[rainfall]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Park|first1=Jeong-Soo|last2=Jung|first2=Hyun-Sook|last3=Kim|first3=Rae-Seon|last4=Oh|first4=Jai-Ho|date=2001|title=Modelling summer extreme rainfall over the Korean peninsula using Wakeby distribution|journal=International Journal of Climatology|language=en|volume=21|issue=11|pages=1371–1384|doi=10.1002/joc.701|bibcode=2001IJCli..21.1371P |s2cid=130799481 |issn=1097-0088|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Su|first1=Buda|last2=Kundzewicz|first2=Zbigniew W.|last3=Jiang|first3=Tong|date=2009-05-01|title=Simulation of extreme precipitation over the Yangtze River Basin using Wakeby distribution|journal=Theoretical and Applied Climatology|language=en|volume=96|issue=3|pages=209–219|doi=10.1007/s00704-008-0025-5|bibcode=2009ThApC..96..209S |s2cid=122488492|issn=1434-4483}}</ref>
* [[tidal current]] speeds,<ref>{{Cite journal|date=2015-10-01|title=Modeling tidal current speed using a Wakeby distribution|journal=Electric Power Systems Research|language=en|volume=127|pages=240–248|doi=10.1016/j.epsr.2015.06.014|issn=0378-7796|last1=Liu|first1=Mingjun|last2=Li|first2=Wenyuan|last3=Billinton|first3=Roy|last4=Wang|first4=Caisheng|last5=Yu|first5=Juan|doi-access=free}}</ref>
* peak [[River flow|flows of rivers]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Öztekin|first=Tekin|date=2011-03-01|title=Estimation of the Parameters of Wakeby Distribution by a Numerical Least Squares Method and Applying it to the Annual Peak Flows of Turkish Rivers|journal=Water Resources Management|language=en|volume=25|issue=5|pages=1299–1313|doi=10.1007/s11269-010-9745-2|s2cid=154960776|issn=1573-1650}}</ref>
* and extreme wind speeds.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Jung |first=Christopher |last2=Schindler |first2=Dirk |last3=Buchholz |first3=Alexander |last4=Laible |first4=Jessica |date=2017 |title=Global Gust Climate Evaluation and Its Influence on Wind Turbines |url=https://doi.org/10.3390/en10101474 |journal=energies |volume=10 |via=MDPI}}</ref>

== Parameters and domain ==
The following restrictions apply to the parameters of this distribution:

*   <math>\beta + \delta \ge 0</math>
*   Either <math>\beta + \delta > 0 </math> or <math>\beta = \gamma = \delta = 0 </math>
*   If <math> \gamma > 0 </math>, then <math>\delta > 0 </math>
*    <math>\gamma \ge 0 </math>
*   <math>\alpha + \gamma \ge 0  </math>

The domain of the Wakeby distribution is

*    <math>\xi </math> to <math>\infty</math>, if <math>\delta \ge 0</math> and <math>\gamma > 0</math>
*    <math>\xi </math> to <math>\xi + (\alpha/ \beta) - (\gamma/ \delta) </math>, if <math>\delta < 0 </math> or <math>\gamma = 0  </math>

With two shape parameters, the Wakeby distribution can model a wide variety of shapes.<ref name="WAKPDF" />

== CDF and PDF ==
The [[cumulative distribution function]] is computed by numerically inverting the quantile function given above. The [[probability density function]] is then found by using the following relation (given on page 46 of Johnson, Kotz, and Balakrishnan<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Johnson|first1=Norman Lloyd|title=Continuous univariate distributions. Vol1|last2=Kotz|first2=Samuel|last3=Balakrishnan|first3=Narayanaswamy|publisher=Wiley|year=1994|isbn=0-471-58495-9|edition=2|location=New York|page=46|oclc=29428092}}</ref>):

:<math>f(x) = \frac{(1 - F(x))^{(\delta+1)}}{\alpha t + \gamma}</math>

where F is the cumulative distribution function and

:<math>t = (1 - F(x))^{(\beta + \delta)}</math>

An implementation that computes the [[probability density function]] of the Wakeby distribution is included in the [[Dataplot]] scientific computation library, as routine WAKPDF.<ref name=WAKPDF/>

An alternative to the above method is to define the PDF parametrically as <math>(W(p),1/w(p)), \ 0\le p \le 1</math>. This can be set up as a [[probability density function]], <math>f(x)</math>, by solving for the unique <math>p</math> in the equation <math>W(p)=x</math> and returning <math>1/w(p)</math>.{{Citation needed|date=June 2021}}
